newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Tuesday on the heels of an uneventful performance in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were tightly mixed in thin directionless trade early Tuesday, with March down three stg at the midday break at 873 stg a tonne, while the remaining months were two stg lower to two stg higher.
London traders brushed aside estimates by commodity brokers GNI which put the Ivorian crop in 1996/97 at 950,000 tonnes leading to a supply deficit of 180,000 tonnes.
In other news, southeast Asian cocoa producers said Tuesday they plan to set up a regional cartel to help insulate them from price volatility and to put them in a better bargaining position.
But Indonesia, the world's third biggest grower, was undecided on whether to join.
Indonesia's cocoa production in 1997 is seen increasing by 10 percent to around 319,000 to 330,000 tonnes, the chairman of the Indonesia Cocoa Association said on Tuesday.
Indonesia's cocoa output reached about 290,000 to 300,000 tonnes in 1996.

Monday, New York March cocoa futures ended narrowly mixed in uneventful trade, with March delivery rising $3 a tonne on the day to $1,336 a tonne after ranging between $1,340 to $1,331. Second-month May firmed $2 to $1,360, while the back months finished up $2 to down $3.

On the charts, traders pegged March near-term resistance at $1,350, then $1,358-$1,360. Support was seen at today's low of $1,331, a double bottom on the charts. The next downside target was put at $1,322, March's life-of-contract low.
